title: Infosys Q2 results, dividend 2026 amount announced:  ₹26 per share payout, profit jumps 6.23% YoY - Check record date | Stock Market News
text:
Infosys Q2 results 2026: Infosys, on Friday, reported a 6.23% annual jump in its consolidated net profit (attributable to owners of the company) to ₹7,832 crore in the September quarter of financial year 2026-27. The IT major also declared an interim dividend of ₹26 per equity share with a face value of ₹5 each.

Infosys share price closed marginally higher on Friday, despite the bearish sentiment prevailing across the Indian stock market. Here are all the details about Infosys Q2 results, dividend announcement and the record date.

The Bengaluru-headquartered IT services firm reported a net profit of ₹7,823 crore in Q2FY27, which is 6.23% higher than ₹7,364 crore reported in the year-ago period.

The company’s net revenue from operations stood at ₹49,244 crore in Q2FY27 against ₹44,490 crore reported in the year-ago period.

The company’s board of directors on Friday considered and approved an interim dividend of ₹26 per share, which is 500% of the stock’s face Value. It has also announced the record date to determine eligibility for the payout and the payment date.

As per Infosys BSE filing, investors must own the stock before the record date, fixed November 3, to become eligible for the payout. The announced dividend is scheduled to be paid by November 11.

Its revenue growth stood at 1.2% on a sequential basis (in constant currency terms), whereas 1.5% on an annual basis (in CC terms). Its operating margin remained stable at 21%. Earnings per share (EPS) growth stood at 8.7% on an annual basis in rupee terms. Total Contract Value (TCV) of large deal wins stood at $5.2 billion, with 62% net new.

In the first half of financial year 2026-27, Infosys’ H1 revenues grew at 1.9% on an annual basis (in CC terms) and its operating margin for H1 stood at 21%.

“We had strong large deals of $5.2 billion, including a mega deal of over $2 billion, reinforcing our position as a trusted partner in the marketplace when clients embark on large and complex transformation programs. Our AI revenue was at 10.5% and grew 29% quarter-on-quarter. As enterprises move to AI adoption at scale, the strong growth in AI revenues is a recognition of our differentiated market positioning and client confidence,” said Salil Parekh, CEO and MD of Infosys.

The company kept its revenue growth guidance at 1%-2% in constant currency terms. Whereas, operating margin is likely to remain near 20%-22%. “We delivered operating margins of 21.0% in Q2 amidst heightened volatility. Focus on cost and operational efficiency measures, while making the required investments, has led to stable margins,” said CFO Jayesh Sanghrajka.
